subject.title: Feature Request: Support YAML as config file format

question: Should OpenClaw accept `openclaw.yaml`/`openclaw.yml` as a second core config file format, or keep `openclaw.json`/JSON5 canonical and solve authoring friction through supported mutation surfaces?
rationale: The request expands a stable on-disk config contract, and automation should not choose parser semantics, file precedence, write-back behavior, or upgrade/doctor expectations without maintainer product ownership.

options.title: Keep JSON5 Canonical
options.body: Treat YAML as out of scope for now and improve docs/tooling around `openclaw config`, Control UI, and `config.patch` for comment-aware edits.

options.title: Sponsor YAML Support
options.body: Accept YAML only with explicit parser, precedence, write-back, docs, fresh-install, upgrade, and doctor proof requirements.

options.title: Split Mutation Guidance
options.body: Track a narrower docs or agent-prompt follow-up for avoiding raw parse-and-dump edits without adding another config format.

recommendation.title: Keep JSON5 Canonical
recommendation.body: Treat YAML as out of scope for now and improve docs/tooling around `openclaw config`, Control UI, and `config.patch` for comment-aware edits.

likelyOwner.reason: The decision is primarily about config compatibility, doctor/recovery behavior, and canonical runtime config policy, where history points most strongly to this owner area.
